findings.reason: §3 should cite the by-type recurrence reader it is distinct from and reuse its counting helper, or state in one line why a second recurrence notion is required.
findings.text: §3 states "no reader of findings by path exists" and cites only `reckon/crew/review.py` as prior art, but `plan_review.py` already reads findings from records and computes their recurrence: `declined_recurrence` (plan_review.py:1421, "counts distinct plans per finding type"), `_finding_type_recurrence` (plan_review.py:1609) and `unanswered_findings` (plan_review.py:1311). §3's recurrence is keyed by file path rather than by finding type, so it is not clearly a duplicate, but the plan does not say so, and the author may re-implement a counting notion that exists one module away

findings.reason: the write path for §5's parser should be `reckon/crew/review.py`, the module that owns the plan-review parser and its rubric item sets, not `plan_review.py`.
findings.text: §5 says the health-review parser is installed "beside the plan-review report parser in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`" and names `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` as its write path, but the parser it means, `parse_plan_review_report`, is at `reckon/crew/review.py:742`, and `plan_review.py:138` itself documents "parser in reckon.crew.review, which owns the names and item sets". Placing a new rubric parser in `plan_review.py` therefore forks the parser family away from its owner; note `plan_review.py` contains no `def parse*` at all

findings.reason: the interface_budget rule requires each section that adds to a family to name what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be; §4 and §6 must each account for the CLI options they add.
findings.text: with `cli_options` 351 this week, §4 adds `dispose --finding <n>` and §6 adds `review --around <plan>` and `--path <path>` (plus keeping `--plan`); §6 accounts for the verb count ("the verb count is unchanged once the plan lands") but no section accounts for the three added options — §4 says only "it adds one option and no verb", and says nothing about what it retires or why nothing can be retired from that family

findings.reason: a removed verb whose callers are not all in the write paths breaks them at the integrated head; §7 must either add these files to its scope or state that they stay on the alias.
findings.text: §7 retires the `review-plan` verb ("which removes §6's alias") but its write paths name only `tests/test_skill_contracts.py` among the tests, while these test modules invoke the verb and are not in any named write path: tests/test_review_plan_command.py:291, tests/test_the_surfaces_pass_the_plan.py:186, tests/test_plan_review_gate.py:672, tests/test_nothing_sweeps_old_plans.py:120, tests/test_an_edit_tells_its_author_a_review_is_owed.py:347. §7's done-when greps only `skills/ reckon/`, so the test callers of the retired verb are uncounted

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/crew/findings.py` hides record reading, scope classification, per-path grouping and recurrence behind one view; §5's parser and §6's composer extend existing modules rather than spreading logic across many small wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 places the new health-review parser "beside the plan-review report parser in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`", but that parser and the names and item sets it owns live in `reckon/crew/review.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — `public_definitions` 1626, `cli_options` 351, `mcp_views` 33, `refusal_families` 23; §3 accounts for its one MCP view ("retires nothing, because no reader of findings by path exists"), but §4 (`dispose --finding`) and §6 (`review --around`, `--path`) add CLI options with no section naming what those options retire or merge, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's reuse map (§2) is real and names the mechanisms it extends, but §3 adds a path-keyed findings reader without citing the findings-recurrence machinery that already exists in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §4 extends the existing `dispose` writer and §6 renames and extends the existing `crew_review_plan` composer rather than layering a parallel verb; the alias is an explicit transition, removed by §7.
